note: Costs are a rough guide for 2 adults + 1 child (summer 2026). Most of the best things on these islands are free — pack for four seasons in a day.

places.name: Old Man of Storr
places.description: Skye's most famous walk — a steep 45–60 minute pull up to the jagged pinnacle and otherworldly Sanctuary, with huge views over Raasay and the Sound.

places.name: The Quiraing
places.description: A landslip landscape of towers, cliffs and hidden plateaus at the north of the Trotternish ridge. Walk the full loop or just wander in from the car park for the views.

places.name: Kilt Rock & Mealt Falls
places.description: Pleated sea cliffs like a hanging kilt, with the Mealt waterfall plunging 55m straight into the sea beside the viewpoint. Two minutes from the car — maximum drama.

places.name: Fairy Glen
places.description: A miniature landslip wonderland of grassy cones, pools and the little 'castle' outcrop above Uig. Easy paths that kids adore — like walking through a model landscape.

places.name: Fairy Pools
places.description: Crystal-blue pools and waterfalls beneath the Black Cuillin. A flat-ish 2.4km walk from the car park; brave souls swim (it is icy, always).

places.name: Neist Point Lighthouse
places.description: Skye's westernmost tip — a concrete path leads out to the 1909 lighthouse under huge cliffs. Watch for whales, dolphins and basking sharks; sunsets are unbeatable.

places.name: Dunvegan Castle & Gardens
places.description: Seat of Clan MacLeod for 800 years — home of the Fairy Flag — with formal gardens and seal-colony boat trips from the jetty below the walls.

places.name: Coral Beach (Claigan)
places.description: A dazzling white 'coral' beach (actually sun-bleached maerl seaweed) at the end of a gentle 20-minute walk from Claigan. Turquoise shallows on a sunny day.

places.name: Talisker Distillery
places.description: Skye's oldest working distillery on the shore of Loch Harport, making the famous maritime malt. Tours are 8+ only, so plan around the wee one — the shop and bar are open to all.

places.name: Elgol & Loch Coruisk boat trip
places.description: The single-track road to Elgol ends at one of Britain's great views; from the jetty, the Misty Isle and Bella Jane boats run into Loch Coruisk past seal colonies, right under the Cuillin.

places.name: Skye Museum of Island Life
places.description: A preserved township of thatched crofts showing island life c.1900. Flora MacDonald's grave is in the cemetery up the hill, looking out to the Outer Hebrides.

places.name: Armadale Castle, Gardens & Museum of the Isles
places.description: Romantic castle ruin, 40 acres of woodland gardens with a great adventure playground, and the excellent Museum of the Isles telling the Clan Donald story. Beside the Mallaig ferry.

places.name: Sligachan Old Bridge
places.description: The classic postcard of the Cuillin, framed by the old stone bridge. Legend says dipping your face in the burn grants eternal beauty — kids love testing it.

places.name: Brother's Point (Rubha nam Brathairean)
places.description: A short, quieter coastal scramble to a grassy headland where dinosaur footprints hide in the shore rocks at low tide — a real-life treasure hunt.

places.name: Dun Beag Broch
places.description: Skye's best-preserved Iron Age broch, a 2,000-year-old drystone tower you can walk into, five minutes up a grassy slope with Loch Bracadale views.

places.name: Blà Bheinn viewpoint (Loch Slapin)
places.description: The marble-white shores of Loch Slapin under Blà Bheinn, the Cuillin outlier. Picnic at the water or, for experienced hikers only, take on the mountain itself.

places.name: Lealt Falls
places.description: A 90m gorge and waterfall with a viewing platform two minutes from the road, plus the remains of a diatomite works by the shore below. An easy leg-stretch on the Trotternish loop.

places.name: Portree Harbour & Scorrybreac walk
places.description: The painted houses of Portree's harbour, then the easy Scorrybreac shore path around the headland — seals, herons and sometimes eagles, ice cream on return.

places.name: Sea eagle boat trip (MV Stardust)
places.description: Short wildlife cruises from Portree pier to the sea-eagle territories of the Sound of Raasay — white-tailed eagles, seals and porpoise most trips.

places.name: Staffin Dinosaur Museum & An Corran footprints
places.description: A tiny croft museum of Jurassic finds from the Staffin coast, then hunt for real dinosaur footprints on An Corran beach at low tide. Peak excitement for small palaeontologists.

places.name: Calanais Standing Stones
places.description: A 5,000-year-old cross of Lewisian gneiss monoliths older than Stonehenge, on a ridge above Loch Roag. Go at dawn or dusk to have them almost to yourself. New visitor centre opens July 2026.

places.name: Gearrannan Blackhouse Village
places.description: A restored crofting township of thatched blackhouses above a stony bay — one is a museum with Harris Tweed weaving demonstrations, another a café.

places.name: Dun Carloway Broch
places.description: One of Scotland's best-preserved brochs, its 9m double wall still standing after 2,000 years. Clamber between the wall passages — free and rarely busy.

places.name: The Blackhouse, Arnol
places.description: Step into a genuine 1880s blackhouse kept exactly as its last family left it in 1966 — peat fire smouldering in the middle of the floor, byre under the same roof.

places.name: Butt of Lewis Lighthouse
places.description: The storm-battered northern full stop of the Hebrides — a Stevenson brick lighthouse over cliffs boiling with seabirds. Officially one of the windiest places in the UK.

places.name: Uig Sands (Tràigh Ùige)
places.description: The immense tidal sands where the Lewis Chessmen were found in 1831 — a giant chess piece sculpture stands guard. At low tide it feels endless.

places.name: Lews Castle & Museum nan Eilean
places.description: Victorian castle in wooded grounds across the harbour, with the free Museum nan Eilean — home to six of the actual Lewis Chessmen. Grounds are great for a run-around.

places.name: Bridge to Nowhere & Tràigh Ghearadha
places.description: Lord Leverhulme's abandoned 1920s concrete bridge, where the road to Ness was never finished, above the gorgeous golden Garry beach and its sea stacks.

places.name: Bosta Iron Age House, Great Bernera
places.description: Cross the 'bridge over the Atlantic' to Bosta beach, where a full reconstruction of the Iron Age houses found under the dunes is open in summer — peat-dark, turf-roofed and atmospheric. A bell rings the time from the shore.

places.name: Norse Mill & Kiln
places.description: Two rebuilt thatched horizontal water mills of Norse design in a fold of moorland — a five-minute walk from the road, and a lovely free glimpse of how crofters ground their barley.

places.name: Eoropie Dunes Park & St Moluag's
places.description: A brilliant community adventure playground in the dunes beside Tràigh Shanndaigh beach, with the medieval chapel of St Moluag nearby — the perfect kid-energy stop near the Butt.

places.name: Whalebone Arch
places.description: The jawbones of an 80-foot blue whale that stranded in 1920, arching over a garden gate on the west-side road — with the harpoon that killed it hanging in the middle.

places.name: Iolaire Memorial
places.description: Moving clifftop memorial to the 201 servicemen lost when HMY Iolaire sank yards from home on New Year's morning 1919 — one of the islands' defining tragedies.

places.name: Reef Beach (Tràigh na Beirghe)
places.description: A perfect crescent of white shell-sand and shallow turquoise water on the Valtos peninsula — one of the best family swimming and paddling beaches on Lewis.

places.name: Mangersta Sea Stacks
places.description: Wild Atlantic cliffs and sea stacks at the island's south-west edge — a short walk from the road, best in a big swell. Keep tight hold of small hands near the edge.

places.name: Abhainn Dearg Distillery
places.description: The Outer Hebrides' first legal whisky distillery in nearly 200 years — a wonderfully home-spun operation making Spirit of Lewis by hand. Tours by arrangement.

places.name: St Columba's Church, Aignish
places.description: Ruined 14th-century church of the Macleods of Lewis on a green headland between two bays, ringed by carved grave slabs — a quiet, atmospheric stop on the way to Point.

places.name: Tiumpan Head Lighthouse
places.description: The best land-based cetacean watchpoint on Lewis — bring binoculars and scan for Risso's dolphins, porpoise and minke whales below the lighthouse.

places.name: Stornoway Harbour & An Lanntair
places.description: Wander the working harbour (seals loaf by the fish quay), then the An Lanntair arts centre for exhibitions, cinema and a café — the islands' cultural hub and a rainy-day banker.

places.name: SeaTrek RIB wildlife trip
places.description: Exhilarating RIB trips from Miavaig pier around Loch Roag's islands and sea caves — seals, eagles and seabirds, with longer runs to remote beaches. Suits kids 5+.

places.name: Luskentyre Beach (Tràigh Losgaintir)
places.description: Regularly voted among the world's best beaches — miles of white sand and impossible blue-green water against the North Harris hills. Sunset here is the trip's highlight.

places.name: Seilebost & Horgabost beaches
places.description: The other side of the Luskentyre estuary — a chain of stunning machair-backed beaches along the A859, each with its own view of Taransay (of Castaway fame).

places.name: Scarista Beach
places.description: Three miles of wild golden sand below the machair golf course — bigger surf and fewer footprints than Luskentyre. Magic in evening light.

places.name: St Clement's Church, Rodel
places.description: The finest medieval church in the Western Isles (c.1520), built for the MacLeod chiefs — climb into the tower and find the remarkable carved tomb of Alasdair Crotach.

places.name: Isle of Harris Distillery
places.description: The 'Social Distillery' by the Tarbert pier — home of the sugar-kelp Harris Gin and The Hearach single malt. Tours daily (12+ only); the canteen fire and shop welcome everyone.

places.name: Harris Tweed Isle of Harris shop
places.description: Floor-to-ceiling bolts of the Orb-stamped cloth in Tarbert's famous tweed shop — and often a loom demonstration. The real thing, woven in islanders' homes.

places.name: The Golden Road (Bays of Harris)
places.description: A twisting single-track lane through the moonscape rock and tiny lochans of Harris's east coast, threading crofting townships from Tarbert to Rodel. Drive it slowly, stop often.

places.name: Eilean Glas Lighthouse, Scalpay
places.description: A moorland path across Scalpay to one of Scotland's first lighthouses (1789), red-banded and standing over the Minch. About an hour's round walk from the trailhead.

places.name: Hushinish Beach
places.description: At the end of the wonderful single-track B887 past Amhuinnsuidhe Castle — a perfect sandy bay looking to the island of Scarp, with a small visitor gateway building.

places.name: North Harris Eagle Observatory
places.description: An open hide up Glen Meavaig in one of Europe's densest golden eagle territories. A flat 30–40 minute walk in; take binoculars and patience.

places.name: An Cliseam (Clisham)
places.description: The highest peak in the Outer Hebrides (799m) — a steep but straightforward pull from the A859 for experienced walkers, with a view over the whole island chain on a clear day.

places.name: Bunavoneader Whaling Station
places.description: The brick chimney and slipways of a Norwegian-built whaling station (1904–1950s) on West Loch Tarbert — an eerie, little-visited piece of Harris history.

places.name: St Kilda day trip
places.description: The big one: a 3-hour crossing from Leverburgh to the abandoned archipelago of St Kilda, a double UNESCO World Heritage Site with a million seabirds. Long day; ages ~10+ advised.

places.name: Seallam! Visitor Centre
places.description: Genealogy and heritage centre where many visitors trace Hebridean ancestors, with a good exhibition on island life and emigration — a fine wet-weather stop in South Harris.

places.name: Talla na Mara & Niseaboist Beach
places.description: Community arts centre on the machair above Niseaboist sands — galleries, events and the Machair Kitchen, with a beautiful, easily-reached beach right below.

places.name: Amhuinnsuidhe Castle & B887 coast road
places.description: The single-track road to Hushinish squeezes right past the front door of this Victorian sporting castle — pull over where the salmon leap the falls beside the gate.

places.name: Tràigh Mheilein
places.description: Often called Britain's most beautiful beach nobody visits — a rough 30–40 minute coastal path north from Hushinish to blinding white sand facing Scarp. Take everything you need.

places.name: Rhenigidale & the Postman's Path
places.description: Once Britain's last roadless village, reached only by boat or the spectacular cliff-cut Postman's Path from Tarbert — walk a stretch of it for wild Minch views.

places.name: Clach Mhic Leòid (MacLeod's Stone)
places.description: A 3m Neolithic standing stone on the headland between Horgabost and Nisabost beaches, perfectly framing Taransay — a two-minute detour with a big payoff.

places.name: Luskentyre Harris Tweed Company
places.description: Visit a working weaver's shed on the Luskentyre road — hear the Hattersley loom clatter and buy tweed woven yards from where you stand. Check opening before calling in.
